# Model diagnostics

To enhance the accuracy, transparency, and replicability of our Bayesian analysis, we used the WAMBS-Checklist to audit and diagnose our models. We will also calculate the residuals for each model and conduct other necessary diagnostics.

## Muscle hypertrophy

Before commencing with the model diagnostics, we will conduct a sensitivity analysis to ensure that the removal of one participant from the data set (due to not adhering to the nutritional requirements of the RT intervention) does not meaningfully affect the results.

```{r}
#| label: Bayesian linear modelling

rf_vl_master_sens <- read_xlsx("Muscle_Thickness/Sensitivity Analysis/rf_vl_master_sens.xlsx")%>%
  mutate_at(c("id","limb","protocol","muscle","sex"),factor)
rf_vl_master_sens=rf_vl_master_sens%>%
  group_by(muscle)%>%
  center(Pre)

# Generate model
MT_model_sens <- brm(muscle.thickness ~ protocol*muscle + Pre + (protocol|id) + (1|id:limb),
                data = rf_vl_master_sens,
                seed = 123,
                control = list(adapt_delta=0.99))
summary(MT_model_sens)

```

Calculate Bayesian estimates generated from the linear model for our sensitivity analysis.

```{r}
#| label: Bayesian estimstes from linear model
                
MT_effects_sens <- emmeans(MT_model_sens, ~ protocol, weights = "prop")
  hpd.summary(MT_effects_sens, point.est = mean) # Display mean
  
MT_effects_contrast_sens <- pairs(emmeans(MT_model_sens, ~ protocol, weights = "prop"))
  hpd.summary(MT_effects_contrast_sens, point.est = mean) # Display mean
  
```

Results are similar between models, the sensitivity analysis model is slightly more in favour of RIR versus FAIL.

We will now move onto the diagnostics. One of our assumptions for the model was that the residuals were normally distributed around zero. We can extract the residuals from the model and plot them to examine this assumption.

```{r}
#| label: Calculate residuals

resid = resid(MT_model)[, "Estimate"]
fit = fitted(MT_model)[, "Estimate"]
ggplot() + geom_point(data = NULL, aes(y = resid, x = fit))

ggplot(dat) + geom_point(aes(y = resid, x = protocol)) # By protocol

```

These plots suggest that the assumption of normally distributed residuals around zero is met.

We will now construct trace plots, histograms, kernel density plots, and autocorrelation plots for parameters of interest. These plots will be presented in the supplementary file.

```{r}
#| label: Diagnostics for muscle hypertrophy

# Trace plot for FAIL
mcmc_trace(MT_model, pars = c("b_Intercept")) + 
  ggplot2::theme(
    axis.text = element_text(
      family = "Helvetica",
      size = 12,
      colour = "black"
    ),
    axis.ticks = element_line(size = 1),
    axis.ticks.length = unit(0.2, "cm"),
    axis.line = element_line(
      size = 1,
      colour = "black",
      linetype = 1
    ),
    panel.background = element_blank()
  ) 

# Trace plot for RIR
mcmc_trace(MT_model, pars = c("b_protocolRIR")) + 
  ggplot2::theme(
    axis.text = element_text(

      colour = "black"
```
